note: Layout Options UI is a submodule of Layout Options. It adds a settings form (route layout_options_ui.settings at /admin/config/system/layout_options/config, permission administer site configuration) that records which layouts should be overridden to use the Layout Options plugin. Choices live in the layout_options.settings config object under layout_overrides, a map keyed by {provider}__{layout_id} with boolean values (core layouts have provider layout_discovery, e.g. layout_discovery__layout_onecol). layout_options_ui_layout_alter() (hook_layout_alter) reads that config and setClass()es each enabled layout to Drupal\layout_options\Plugin\Layout\LayoutOptions. No plugins/permissions/Drush of its own. Medium/hard cases are grounded in the raw layout_overrides config (the cause), distinct from the parent module's cases which verify the resulting layout-plugin class (the effect). Baseline layout_overrides is empty, restored explicitly.

evals.prompt: Where does Layout Options UI store which layouts are overridden to use Layout Options, and what is the config route to manage it?
evals.expected_output: It stores them in the layout_options.settings config object under the layout_overrides key. The admin form is route layout_options_ui.settings at /admin/config/system/layout_options/config (permission administer site configuration).

evals.prompt: In Layout Options UI's layout_overrides config, what is the format of each key that identifies a layout to override? Give the example for the core one-column layout.
evals.expected_output: Each key is {provider}__{layout_id}. Core layouts are provided by layout_discovery, so the core one-column layout's key is layout_discovery__layout_onecol; the value is 1/true to override it.

evals.prompt: How does Layout Options UI actually make an existing layout use the Layout Options plugin once it is enabled in the config?
evals.expected_output: layout_options_ui_layout_alter() (a hook_layout_alter implementation) reads layout_options.settings layout_overrides and, for each enabled {provider}__{layout_id}, calls $definition->setClass('\Drupal\layout_options\Plugin\Layout\LayoutOptions'). Clearing the layout plugin cache applies it.

evals.prompt: Inspect this site's layout_options.settings configuration and tell me which layout is currently marked to be overridden by Layout Options UI.
evals.expected_output: The layout_onecol layout: layout_options.settings layout_overrides contains layout_discovery__layout_onecol => 1.

evals.prompt: Read the Layout Options UI override configuration on this site and give me the exact config key (including provider prefix) that is currently enabled in layout_overrides.
evals.expected_output: The enabled key is layout_discovery__layout_twocol (set to 1) in layout_options.settings layout_overrides.

evals.prompt: Using Layout Options UI, configure the live site so that the core one-column layout (layout_onecol) is marked to be overridden with Layout Options.
evals.expected_output: Set layout_options.settings layout_overrides['layout_discovery__layout_onecol'] = 1 (via the form at /admin/config/system/layout_options/config, or the config API). The stored config value for that key is then 1.

evals.prompt: Configure Layout Options UI on the live site so the core two-column layout (layout_twocol) is enabled for a Layout Options override.
evals.expected_output: Set layout_options.settings layout_overrides['layout_discovery__layout_twocol'] = 1 (via the settings form or config API). The stored config value for layout_discovery__layout_twocol is then 1.
